paper1.title: Practical Defaults and Checks for Studies of Foundation Model Features
rows: **Practical defaults**
Which size comparator?
LUNA25-Dev: selected FM setup 0.82 (0.80, 0.85), diameter 0.82 (0.80, 0.85), Brock model 0.83 (0.81, 0.85)
Report diameter and nodule type, and the Brock model in screening data, beside every FM result
How much model search?
One encoder chosen by its rank in the other tasks, with logistic regression, minus the full search: AUC difference +0.002 (−0.025, 0.027) (companion article [35])
Start with a simple model setup and state how it was chosen
Which no-pretraining control?
Model setups with a higher AUC than a random-weight encoder in external screening and suspicion cohorts: 90.0% (78.6%, 94.4%)
Use a random-weight encoder to show that pretrained features carry signal, not that the model is clinically useful
**Four checks before claiming an improvement**
1. An external test cohort
External test minus within-cohort AUC of the same model setups: −0.031 (−0.044, −0.022) (companion article [35])
Evaluate in a cohort that played no part in model training or model choice
2. Diameter as the size comparator
LIDC-path: diameter-only logistic model fitted in the other cohorts 0.27 (0.15, 0.41), diameter 0.73 (0.59, 0.85)
Report diameter (larger = more suspicious) beside any fitted diameter-only logistic model
3. The range expected by chance in cohorts under about 150 nodules
LUNGx (79 nodules): selected FM setup 0.56 (0.43, 0.69), inside the range expected by chance (0.38 to 0.63)
Show the label-permutation range; call results inside it not distinguished from chance
4. A model chosen without test labels
Model setup with the highest test AUC minus the selected FM setup: median 0.048 (companion article [35])
Choose the model setup in training data; never report the best test result as the estimate

paper1b.title: Summary of Findings and Suggested Starting Points
rows: Which encoder? †
6 of 18 encoders above the random-weight encoder in external testing; mean rank 2.9 (2.3, 5.2) for Pillar0-ChestCT and 3.4 (2.5, 5.4) for Pillar0-Sybil-1.5, with overlapping intervals
Start from one strong chest CT encoder; read rank intervals, not a single ranking
Which feature form?
Whole crop vs default feature form in external testing, −0.013 (−0.023, −0.004) with logistic regression and −0.023 (−0.034, −0.011) with LightGBM
Avoid pooling over the whole crop; gains from narrower windows were not consistent
Which classifier?
Classifier share of AUC variance in external testing, 0.6%; TabPFN vs logistic regression, −0.009 (−0.015, −0.001)
Use L2-regularized logistic regression
Attention-based classifiers or fusion? †
Features of two encoders joined vs selected FM setup in external testing, −0.044 (−0.078, −0.009)
No evidence of benefit
Full search or a fixed choice? †
One encoder chosen by rank in the other tasks minus full search, +0.002 (−0.025, 0.027); lower in 2 of 4 screening and suspicion tasks
Start from one strong encoder; check it against a small search
How optimistic is the best result found? †
Setup chosen with test labels a median 0.048 AUC above the selected FM setup (no CI); not above the permutation null of the maximum in three small pathology cohorts
Select in training data only; report the range expected by chance in small cohorts (here, under 100 nodules)
Will a within-cohort result hold? †
External test minus within-cohort AUC, same model setups, −0.031 (−0.044, −0.022)
Report AUC in a separate cohort; read within-cohort AUC as optimistic
Will an encoder ranking carry over?
Kendall τ between settings, 0.61 to 0.88 in screening and suspicion and −0.27 to 0.66 in pathology tasks
Recheck the ranking in the target population
How many training cases? †
At 25 cases per class, median encoder minus diameter alone, −0.249 to −0.128 in screening and suspicion tasks
With a small development set, compare with diameter alone
